title: Nonspecial divisor in the smooth locus of a nodal curve
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-pc-separably-closed] and let $X/k$ be a nonempty projective geometrically reduced geometrically connected curve [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] with nodal geometric fibres [def-kun-projective, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Put $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, with coherent cohomology [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. There is an effective Cartier divisor $E$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] supported in the smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], of degree $g$, such that $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X(E))=0$ and the canonical inclusion $k\to H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(E))$ is an isomorphism. The divisor can be chosen to be a sum of $g$ distinct $k$-rational smooth points. For $g=0$ it is the empty divisor. Degree means $\chi(\mathcal O_X(E))-\chi(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic].

source.place: Lemma 4.4, printed p.143; successive independent evaluations of the dualizing sheaf at smooth points. The distinctness refinement follows by avoiding the finitely many previously chosen points. Primary Numdam PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence finite type and separated. Over the Noetherian field $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian and [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally finitely presented; quasi-compactness and separatedness give finite presentation. It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. The nodal curve hypotheses give pure dimension one on its geometric fibres: a zero-dimensional irreducible component of a reduced finite-type curve is an isolated open-and-closed point, contrary to connectedness and dimension one; the other components have dimension one. The same applies to $X$. By [lem-pc-projective-coherent-finiteness] coherent cohomology is finite-dimensional, and [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>1$. By [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected], the canonical $k\to H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is an isomorphism. Thus $g$ is finite and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g$.

source.place: Tag 0BS2, lemma-duality-dim-1, proper-curve setup; varieties.tex Tag 0BUG, global functions; cohomology.tex Tag 02UZ. Deligne Lemma 4.4, Riemann--Roch setup.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] to $f$. Step 1 checked properness, flatness and finite presentation, and the assumed nodal geometric fibres satisfy its remaining hypotheses. It supplies an invertible dualizing sheaf $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module] to $X$: it supplies the natural duality isomorphism and uniqueness of the representing pair. Since $W$ represents the same functor, identify it with $\omega_X$ through this uniqueness. Taking $F=\mathcal O_X$, the identity $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)=\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$ gives $\dim_k\Gamma(X,\omega_X)=g$. We will also use the cited module theorem's assertion that a morphism to $\omega_X$ vanishing at every component-generic stalk is zero.

source.place: Tag 0E6R, lemma-gorenstein-dualizing and preceding field-case representing property; curves.tex Tags 0BS2, 0BS3. Deligne Lemma 4.4, dualizing sheaf.

proof.text: Let $U$ be the smooth locus. It is dense by [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open]. For any nonzero $s\in\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$ and finite set $T$ of smooth rational points, the map $\mathcal O_X\to\omega_X$ defined by $s$ is nonzero at some component-generic stalk by step 2. Trivialize the invertible sheaf near that generic point. Its representing function has nonzero residue in the generic field; after restriction to its principal nonvanishing open it is a unit. That open meets $U$, and deleting $T$ still leaves a nonempty open: its generic point has dimension-one closure and is not one of the finitely many closed points in $T$. This is a nonempty smooth $k$-scheme. By [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], it contains a $k$-rational point $P$. At $P$ the evaluation $s(P)\in\omega_X\otimes k(P)$ is nonzero, and $P\notin T$.

source.place: Tags 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open), 056U (lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense); Deligne Lemma 4.4, choice of a smooth point. Distinctness: delete the previous finite set.

proof.text: Construct distinct $P_1,\ldots,P_g\in U(k)$ inductively. Let $V_0=\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$ and, after $i$ choices, let $V_i$ be the subspace of sections evaluating to zero at all $P_1,\ldots,P_i$. Inductively $\dim_k V_i=g-i$. If $i<g$, choose $0\ne s\in V_i$ and apply step 3 with $T=\{P_1,\ldots,P_i\}$ to choose $P_{i+1}$ where $s$ is nonzero. Evaluation $V_i\to\omega_X\otimes k(P_{i+1})$ is therefore nonzero. Its target is one-dimensional because $\omega_X$ is invertible and $k(P_{i+1})=k$, so its image has dimension one and its kernel $V_{i+1}$ has dimension $g-i-1$. This proves the induction and gives $V_g=0$. If $g=0$, no choices are made and already $V_0=0$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, printed p.143: induction on independent evaluations; finite-dimensional rank-nullity written explicitly, with avoidance of previous points.

proof.text: Let $E$ be the reduced union of the $P_i$ in $X$. Each $k$-rational point is closed because $X/k$ is separated, and $E\cong\coprod_{i=1}^g\operatorname{Spec}k$. The smooth locus $U$ has relative dimension one: its components lie in the dimension-one components of $X$; the nodal curve has no isolated components by step 1. The finite locally free closed subscheme $E\subset U$ is an effective Cartier divisor by [lem-pc-cartier-criterion]. The effective Cartier property extends to $X$ on the cover $U\cup(X\setminus E)$, with local equation $1$ on the second open. Thus $E$ is a sum of distinct smooth rational points. Its associated module $M=\mathcal O_X(E)$ is invertible by [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties]. By [lem-pc-degree-base-change], $\deg M=\dim_k\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)=g$. This includes the empty union for $g=0$, whose ideal is $\mathcal O_X$ and whose degree is zero.

source.place: Tag 0B9D, lemma-divisors-on-curves, (1) implies (2), on the smooth open; varieties.tex Tag 0AYY, lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor. Deligne Lemma 4.4, divisor construction.

proof.text: Write $I=\mathcal I_E$; by definition $M=I^\vee$. The canonical inclusion $\mathcal O_X\to M$ is locally the injective map $a\mapsto ta$ in a trivialization where $I=(t)$ and $t$ is a nonzerodivisor. Precomposition identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\omega_X)$ with the global sections of $I\otimes\omega_X$ inside $\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$: in the same trivialization it is multiplication by $t$. At each reduced smooth point $P_i$, membership in $I\otimes\omega_X$ is exactly zero evaluation modulo its maximal ideal; away from $E$ the ideal is the unit ideal. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\omega_X)=V_g=0$. By the natural isomorphism of [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module], the dual of $H^1(X,M)$ is zero. This cohomology is finite-dimensional by step 1, so $H^1(X,M)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BS2, lemma-duality-dim-1 (5); rank-one Hom calculation as in Tag 0BS4, remark-rework-duality-locally-free. Deligne Lemma 4.4, duality criterion.

proof.text: By step 1, $\chi(X,M)=h^0(X,M)-h^1(X,M)=h^0(X,M)$. Using the degree convention of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] and [def-pc-euler-characteristic], steps 1 and 5 give $h^0(X,M)=\deg M+\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=g+1-g=1$. The injective sheaf map $\mathcal O_X\to M$ from step 6 sends $1$ to a nonzero global section: locally its image is the nonzerodivisor $t$ and $X$ is nonempty. Hence the resulting canonical map $k\to H^0(X,M)$ is injective. Both vector spaces have dimension one, so it is an isomorphism. When $g=0$ the construction took $E=\varnothing$, $M=\mathcal O_X$, and all these assertions reduce to $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ and the canonical global-functions isomorphism from step 1.

The Deligne Lemma 4.4 PDF is not in the local literature: the report files a WANTED line and proof_origin.by is agent, so I checked the proof as a self-contained argument. Step 1: proper, Noetherian, finitely presented, flat; finite coherent cohomology; H^{>=2}=0; H^0(O)=k from properness, geometric reducedness and geometric connectedness. The pure-dimension-one argument (a zero-dimensional component would be a clopen point) is correct. Step 2: the relative Gorenstein node applies to f over Spec k, and the reduced-curve node's uniqueness clause identifies its sheaf with omega_X, so omega_X is invertible with dim Gamma(omega)=g. Step 3: the generic-stalk clause, a principal open, density of the smooth locus and rational-point density over the separably closed field give a rational smooth point P outside T with s(P) nonzero. Step 4: the rank-nullity induction is elementary and correct. Step 5: the Cartier criterion (1)=>(2) applies on U, which is smooth of relative dimension 1, and the degree is g by the degree node's clause 2 as currently stated. Step 6: Hom(M,omega) equals V_g, which is 0, so H^1(M)=0 by duality. Step 7: Euler-characteristic rearrangement plus injectivity of the constants map. Small cases checked: P^1, the nodal cubic, two P^1 meeting twice, a tree of P^1's. The statement is unchanged apart from added definition citations, there are no new nodes, and there is no duplicate in the DAG. No re-split note exists for this item.
